figures.caption: Figure 1: Raw EEG record with artifacts (black trace) and the same data after artifact correction (red trace), demonstrating the improvement in signal quality achievable with proper preprocessing.

Table 1: Common EEG artifact types and their typical removal approaches. Preferred methods reflect widely used practices in EEG preprocessing; alternative strategies may be appropriate depending on data quality, recording setup, and research objectives.

Figure 2: Representative EEG recordings across acquisition conditions. (A) Outside scanner room, (B) Inside scanner bore with no imaging sequence running (Scanner OFF), (C) Active imaging sequence (Scanner ON) showing high-amplitude gradient artifact, and (D) Final cleaned data after sequential gradient and pulse artifact correction. Reproduced from Razmara et al. (2026).

Figure 4: Example of low-dimensional latent neural trajectories during a reaching task (adapted from [94]). Neural population activity projected onto jPC1 and jPC2 exhibits structured rotational dynamics.

Figure 5: Example of time-resolved decoding during a cognitive task. Decodability over time indicates when neural representations differ between processing distinct sentences or producing different behavioral responses [97].
